title: The formats you will meet most often

blocks.what_we_do: Read fields in tiny invented examples. Conversion commands below are examples to read, not instructions to run.
blocks.why:
All files in [examples/formats](../examples/formats/) are labelled **invented example**. S1 to S4 are invented identifiers. S1 is male, S2 and S4 are female, and S3 has unknown sex. Five two-allele SNPs use invented GRCh38-style positions on chromosomes 1, 2 and X. One genotype is missing. S1 has a [haploid](../docs/glossary.md#haploid) X call, with one allele copy, outside the [pseudoautosomal regions](../docs/glossary.md#pseudoautosomal-region), the X/Y regions that pair. Two reads belong to a separate invented 60-base contig, `toy1`. These files cannot support a biological conclusion.

A [header](../docs/glossary.md#header) describes a file before its data records. [Magic bytes](../docs/glossary.md#magic-bytes) are byte patterns that identify some binary encodings. The binary examples have companion `.hex.txt` files showing their first bytes. Every JSON description retains the label "invented example". File names use underscores. Binary headers cannot accept arbitrary comments.

**FASTQ.** Open [the read example](../examples/formats/invented_example_reads.fastq). Each record has four lines: `@` plus identifier, sequence, `+`, and qualities. [Phred quality](../docs/glossary.md#phred-quality) expresses base-error probability. Here each `I` means 40 under Phred+33 encoding. Quality length must equal sequence length. A common mistake is to confuse these base qualities with alignment confidence. Alignment software converts reads into SAM or BAM using a reference.

**SAM/BAM/CRAM.** Read [the SAM example](../examples/formats/invented_example_alignments.sam) beside [FASTA](../examples/formats/invented_example_reference.fasta) and [FAI](../examples/formats/invented_example_reference.fasta.fai). `@HD` declares version and sorting; `@SQ` declares reference name and length; `@CO` is a comment. The eleven required fields are `QNAME` (read name), `FLAG` (encoded alignment properties), `RNAME` (reference name), `POS` (one-based start), `MAPQ` (mapping confidence), `CIGAR` (alignment operations), `RNEXT` and `PNEXT` (mate reference and position), `TLEN` (template length), `SEQ` (read bases) and `QUAL` (base qualities). Optional `TAG:TYPE:VALUE` fields add annotations. A [CIGAR](../docs/glossary.md#cigar) such as `4M1I5M` means four aligned bases, one inserted read base, then five aligned bases. `M` does not distinguish matches from mismatches. The example reads are unpaired, so mate fields are absent or zero. [Bit flags](../docs/glossary.md#bit-flag) combine properties in one integer; zero here means an unpaired forward alignment. BAM stores the same logical fields in binary. CRAM may require the exact reference used to encode it. Mixing references or reusing an old index gives incorrect retrieval or errors.

Read-only shell example:

```sh
samtools view -b -o reads.bam reads.sam
samtools sort -o sorted.bam reads.bam
samtools index sorted.bam
```

`view -b` writes BAM; `-o` names the output. `sort` orders alignments by coordinate. `index` creates the companion region index. The filenames here are explanatory names, not supplied exercise inputs. Calling variants from BAM/CRAM needs a suitable caller and study design; format conversion alone does not call variants.

**VCF/gVCF.** Read [the multi-sample VCF](../examples/formats/invented_example_multisample.vcf), [gVCF](../examples/formats/invented_example_sample.g.vcf) and [dosage VCF](../examples/formats/invented_example_dosages.vcf). `##` lines declare metadata. The columns are `CHROM` (chromosome), `POS` (one-based position), `ID` (variant identifier), `REF` (reference allele), `ALT` (alternative alleles), `QUAL` (variant quality), `FILTER` (filter status), `INFO` (site annotations), `FORMAT` (sample-field order), then one column per sample. A dot is missing. `PASS` says no listed filter failed; it does not prove a correct call. [GT](../docs/glossary.md#vcf-genotype) uses allele indices: `0/1` means REF/first ALT, while `./.` is missing. A slash leaves the parental order unknown; a vertical bar records [phase](../docs/glossary.md#phasing), which alleles belong together on a chromosome copy. The gVCF uses `<NON_REF>` and `END` to describe a reference block. It is an illustrative convention, not a complete caller output for joint calling. [DS](../docs/glossary.md#dosage) is the expected ALT count. [GP](../docs/glossary.md#genotype-probability) gives genotype probabilities; for diploid calls, their order is `0/0,0/1,1/1`. Thus `DS = GP(0/1) + 2 * GP(1/1)`. For S1 on X, GP instead lists `0,1` and DS equals GP(1). `R2` is a declared imputation-quality annotation. Its exact definition depends on the producer; the example value is invented. Do not replace uncertain dosages with rounded calls without a reason.

Read-only shell example:

```sh
plink2 --vcf "invented_example_multisample.vcf" --double-id --update-sex "invented_example_plink2.psam" --make-pgen --out converted
```

`--vcf` selects the input. `--double-id` sets both PLINK identifiers from each sample name. `--update-sex` reads the named sex column. `--make-pgen` creates the native trio; `--out` names its shared prefix. This example retains calls. Importing dosage values additionally requires the documented `dosage=DS` modifier to `--vcf`. A conversion preserves supplied alleles; it does not validate their reference build.

**Illumina Final Report, IDAT and GTC.** Open [the Final Report example](../examples/formats/invented_example_final_report.txt). `[Header]` gives file information; `[Data]` begins the selected columns. `SNP Name` identifies a marker; `Sample ID` identifies a sample; `Allele1 - Forward` and `Allele2 - Forward` are called alleles on the declared strand. `GC Score` is calling confidence, not a disease probability. `X` and `Y` are illustrative normalised intensities. Missing calls use `-` here. Actual exports offer other columns and conventions. IDAT contains earlier scanner intensities. GTC contains binary calls and related measurements. No vendor binary is fabricated. The next conversion needs the exact export columns and the matching manifest. A universal text-import command would hide those choices. See [2.5](module_02_files_and_formats.Rmd#step-2-5) before interpreting strand labels.

**PLINK 1 and PLINK 2.** Read [PED](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1.ped), [MAP](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1.map), [TPED](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1_transposed.tped), [TFAM](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1_transposed.tfam), [BIM](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1.bim), [FAM](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1.fam), [PVAR](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink2.pvar) and [PSAM](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink2.psam). FAM/TFAM and the first six PED fields are family ID, individual ID, father ID, mother ID, sex and phenotype. Zero parent IDs mean unknown; sex is 1 male, 2 female and 0 unknown in FAM. Phenotype `-9` is missing. PED then gives two alleles per variant; `0 0` is a missing call. MAP columns are chromosome, variant ID, genetic distance and one-based position. TPED starts with these four variant fields, then allele pairs per sample. BIM adds allele 1 and allele 2 to MAP's four fields. The binary [BED](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink1.bed) starts `6c 1b 01` in this variant-major encoding. Sample and variant order come from its companions. PLINK 1.9 often treats A1/A2 as minor/major in analysis; those are sample-frequency labels, not genomic REF/ALT. PVAR instead names `CHROM, POS, ID, REF, ALT`; this example also has `FILTER`. PSAM names `FID, IID, SEX` in its header; `NA` means unknown sex. [PGEN](../examples/formats/invented_example_plink2.pgen) starts `6c 1b`, followed by its storage-mode information. A reference allele imported from an old BIM may remain provisional. Do not silently assume it matches GRCh38.

Read-only shell example:

```sh
plink2 --bfile invented_example_plink1 --make-pgen --out converted
```

`--bfile` reads the BED/BIM/FAM trio with that prefix. `--make-pgen` creates PGEN/PVAR/PSAM; `--out` sets the new prefix. Keep every trio together. Do not mix companion files from separate runs.

**BGEN.** Inspect [the BGEN bytes](../examples/formats/invented_example.bgen.hex.txt) and [sample table](../examples/formats/invented_example.sample). The binary header records variant/sample counts and encoding flags. The `bgen` signature occurs at byte offset 16. Variant records identify the chromosome, position, alleles and encoded probabilities. Layout 2 supports different allele counts and numbers of chromosome copies. Our BGEN 1.2 uses eight bits per probability and represents called genotypes as certainty, not genuine imputation. Its sample table has `ID_1`, `ID_2`, `missing` and `sex`. The second row declares column types. A missingness value is descriptive; it is not a reason to replace formal QC. Read [the specification](https://www.chg.ox.ac.uk/~gav/bgen_format/spec/v1.2.html) before decoding binary records.

Read-only shell example:

```sh
plink2 --bgen "invented_example.bgen" ref-first --sample "invented_example.sample" --make-pgen --out converted
```

`--bgen` selects the file. `ref-first` declares that this example's first allele is the reference. `--sample` supplies the companion sample table. Do not assume the same allele order for an unfamiliar BGEN file.

**Summary statistics.** Open [the example table](../examples/formats/invented_example_summary_statistics.tsv). `chromosome`, `base_pair_location` and `variant_id` locate and name the variant. `effect_allele` is the allele whose effect is reported; `other_allele` is its partner. `effect_allele_frequency` is its fraction among called alleles. `odds_ratio` describes the effect on disease [odds](../docs/glossary.md#odds), the probability of disease divided by the probability of no disease. `beta` is its [natural logarithm](../docs/glossary.md#logarithm). `standard_error` measures [uncertainty in beta](../docs/glossary.md#standard-error). `p_value` measures evidence against the tested [null model](../docs/glossary.md#null-hypothesis), which assumes no association. `n` is the number of samples with a called genotype in this example. Effects and uncertainties are invented, not fitted to four samples. Step 6.8 creates the classroom table. [GWAS-SSF requirements](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/docs/summary-statistics-format/) additionally specify fields and study metadata for submission. Never interpret beta without its effect allele, scale and build.

**References:** [FASTQ, PMID 20015970](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20015970/); [SAM/BAM, PMID 19505943](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19505943/); [CRAM, PMID 21245279](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21245279/); [CRAM 3.1, PMID 34999766](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34999766/); [VCF, PMID 21653522](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21653522/); [GATK, PMID 20644199](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20644199/); [PLINK, PMID 17701901](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17701901/); [second-generation PLINK, PMID 25722852](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25722852/); [SAMtools/BCFtools, PMID 33590861](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33590861/); [BGEN, DOI 10.1101/308296](https://doi.org/10.1101/308296).
blocks.you_need: Step 1.9 and the linked invented examples. Their JSON descriptions in `site_content/formats/` explain every example field. No classroom data or password is needed.
blocks.command: No code to run. This is a reading-only step. The shell examples in Why show conversion syntax only.
blocks.expected_result: You can explain the header and fields of each example. The offline generator verifies that PLINK imports preserve the five variants, four samples and one missing genotype across the supplied genotype formats.
blocks.troubleshooting: A binary file will not look like a readable table. Use its JSON description and hex dump. The illustrative conversion outputs are not needed for any later step.
blocks.quick_check:
An imputed sample has probabilities `0.1, 0.8, 0.1`. What is its ALT dosage, and is that a certain heterozygous call?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The dosage is `0.8 + 2 * 0.1 = 1`. It is not certainty: the two homozygous possibilities still have probability 0.1 each.

</details>
